--- title: "Probability and Statistics Review 📊" subtitle: "MATH 4750 / MSSC 5750 Computational Statistics" format: revealjs: code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" highlight-style: arrow code-block-bg: true self-contained: false slide-number: c/t incremental: false width: 1800 height: 1000 margin: 0.05 logo: "logo.png" footer: "[mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27](https://mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27/)" theme: ["simple", "slides.scss"] multiplex: false code-link: true fig-cap-location: bottom fig-align: center transition: none ## fade slide convex concave zoom title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: mu-bg.png data-background-size: stretch data-slide-number: none editor: source execute: freeze: auto echo: true purl: true --- # {visibility="hidden"} \def\bx{\mathbf{x}} \def\by{\mathbf{y}} \def\bz{\mathbf{z}} \def\bu{\mathbf{u}} \def\bv{\mathbf{v}} \def\bw{\mathbf{w}} \def\bX{\mathbf{X}} \def\bY{\mathbf{Y}} \def\bZ{\mathbf{Z}} \def\bU{\mathbf{U}} \def\bV{\mathbf{V}} \def\bW{\mathbf{W}} \def\bI{\mathbf{I}} \def\bH{\mathbf{H}} \def\bS{\mathbf{S}} \def\bD{\mathbf{D}} \def\bbeta{\boldsymbol \beta} \def\btheta{\boldsymbol \theta} \def\bmu{\boldsymbol \mu} \def\bSigma{\boldsymbol \Sigma} \def\bLambda{\boldsymbol \Lambda} \def\beps{\boldsymbol \epsilon} \def\T{\text{T}} \def\E{\mathrm{E}} \def\var{\mathrm{Var}} \def\cov{\mathrm{Cov}} \def\cor{\mathrm{Corr}} \def\se{\mathrm{se}} \def\bias{\mathrm{bias}} \def\mse{\mathrm{MSE}} \def\R{\mathbb{R}} \def\P{\mathrm{P}} \def\iid{\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{arg\,min} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{arg\,max} # Probability and Statistics Review

Random variables, moments, and conditional expectation

Discrete and continuous families in R

Multivariate normal and limit theorems

Statistics: ecdf, quantiles, bias, MSE, MLE

Bayes' theorem and Markov chains

::: notes - Rizzo Chapter 2. Throughout the semester we will verify every theoretical statement by simulation; this chapter is the first place we start doing that. ::: ## Random Variables and Moments (Rizzo 2.1) - cdf $F_X(x) = P(X\le x)$: non-decreasing, right-continuous, $\lim_{x\to-\infty}F = 0$, $\lim_{x\to\infty}F=1$ - Discrete: pmf $f_X(x) = P(X=x)$; continuous: pdf $f_X(x) = F_X'(x)$ - $\E[X] = \int x\, dF(x)$, $\var(X) = \E[(X-\mu)^2] = \E[X^2] - \mu^2$ - $\cov(X,Y) = \E[(X-\mu_X)(Y-\mu_Y)]$, $\rho(X,Y) = \dfrac{\cov(X,Y)}{\sigma_X\sigma_Y}$ ::: alert Uncorrelated does **not** imply independent, except when $(X, Y)$ is jointly normal. ::: - For iid $X_1,\dots,X_n$: $\E[\bar X] = \mu$, $\var(\bar X) = \sigma^2/n$. ## Conditional Expectation Rule and Conditional Variance Formula $$ \E[X] = \E\big[\E[X\mid Y]\big] \qquad (2.1) $$ $$ \var(X) = \E\big[\var(X\mid Y)\big] + \var\big(\E[X\mid Y]\big) \qquad (2.2) $$ **Example (Poisson-Gamma mixture).** $X\mid \Lambda \sim\text{Poisson}(\Lambda)$, $\Lambda\sim\text{Gamma}(r, \beta)$. - (2.1): $\E[X] = \E[\Lambda] = r/\beta$ - (2.2): $\var(X) = \E[\Lambda] + \var(\Lambda) = r/\beta + r/\beta^2$ . . . ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750) r <- 4; beta <- 2; n <- 1e5 lambda <- rgamma(n, shape = r, rate = beta) x <- rpois(n, lambda) rbind(simulation = c(mean = mean(x), var = var(x)), formulas = c(r / beta, r / beta + r / beta^2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean var simulation 1.997 3.003 formulas 2.000 3.000 ``` ::: ::: ::: notes - This mixture is the negative binomial distribution: X ~ NegBin(r, p = beta/(1+beta)). Check with dnbinom. - HW 1 asks you to do exactly this for two other hierarchical models. ::: ## The Mixture Is Negative Binomial ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} k <- 0:12 obs <- as.numeric(table(factor(x, levels = k))) / n barplot(rbind(obs, dnbinom(k, size = r, prob = beta / (1 + beta))), beside = TRUE, names.arg = k, col = c("#FFCC00", "#003366"), legend.text = c("simulated", "NegBin(4, 2/3)"), main = "Poisson-Gamma mixture") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Some Discrete Distributions (Rizzo 2.2) :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - **Binomial** $X\sim\text{Bin}(n,p)$: number of successes in $n$ Bernoulli trials; $np$, $np(1-p)$ - **Multinomial**: counts in $k$ categories - **Geometric**: $P(X = x) = p q^x$, $x=0,1,\dots$ (failures before first success); cdf $1-q^{x+1}$ (Example 2.1) - **Negative binomial** $(r,p)$: failures before $r$th success; $\binom{x+r-1}{r-1}p^rq^x$ (2.6) - **Poisson$(\lambda)$**: $e^{-\lambda}\lambda^x/x!$; mean = variance = $\lambda$ (Example 2.2) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) k <- 0:15 plot(k, dbinom(k, 15, .4), type = "h", lwd = 5, main = "Bin(15, .4)", ylab = "") plot(k, dgeom(k, .25), type = "h", lwd = 5, main = "Geom(.25)", ylab = "") plot(k, dnbinom(k, 3, .4), type = "h", lwd = 5, main = "NegBin(3, .4)", ylab = "") plot(k, dpois(k, 4), type = "h", lwd = 5, main = "Poisson(4)", ylab = "") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Some Continuous Distributions (Rizzo 2.3) - **Normal** $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$: $Z = (X-\mu)/\sigma\sim N(0,1)$ - **Gamma$(r,\lambda)$**: $f(x) = \frac{\lambda^r}{\Gamma(r)} x^{r-1}e^{-\lambda x}$; Exponential = Gamma$(1,\lambda)$; $\chi^2(\nu)$ = Gamma$(\nu/2, 1/2)$ - **Beta$(\alpha,\beta)$** on $(0,1)$; Uniform(0,1) = Beta(1,1) - **Lognormal**: $\log X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$ - **Student $t(\nu)$** $= Z/\sqrt{V/\nu}$, **$F(\nu_1,\nu_2)$** $= (U/\nu_1)/(V/\nu_2)$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); z <- rnorm(1e5); v <- rchisq(1e5, df = 5) tt <- z / sqrt(v / 5) rbind(quantile(tt, c(.9, .95, .99)), qt(c(.9, .95, .99), df = 5)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 90% 95% 99% [1,] 1.493 2.037 3.383 [2,] 1.476 2.015 3.365 ``` ::: ::: ## Memoryless Exponential (Examples 2.3 - 2.4) $$ P(X > s + t \mid X > s) = \frac{e^{-\lambda(s+t)}}{e^{-\lambda s}} = e^{-\lambda t} = P(X>t). $$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2027); x <- rexp(1e6, rate = 0.5); s <- 2; t <- 3 c(conditional = mean(x[x > s] > s + t), unconditional = mean(x > t), exact = exp(-0.5 * t)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` conditional unconditional exact 0.2233 0.2236 0.2231 ``` ::: ::: - **Two-parameter exponential** with location $\eta$: $F(x) = 1 - e^{-\lambda(x-\eta)}$, $x\ge\eta$ (shift a standard exponential). ## Multivariate Normal (Rizzo 2.4) $$ f(\bx) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}|\bSigma|^{1/2}}\exp\left\{-\tfrac12(\bx-\bmu)^\T\bSigma^{-1}(\bx-\bmu)\right\} $$ - Marginals and conditionals of a MVN are normal; linear transformations $\mathbf{A}\bX+\mathbf{b}\sim N(\mathbf{A}\bmu+\mathbf{b}, \mathbf{A}\bSigma\mathbf{A}^\T)$ - If $\bZ\sim N_d(\mathbf 0, \bI)$ and $\bSigma = \mathbf{C}\mathbf{C}^\T$, then $\bX = \bmu + \mathbf{C}\bZ \sim N_d(\bmu,\bSigma)$ (**Ch 3!**) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} Sigma <- matrix(c(1, .8, .8, 1), 2); C <- t(chol(Sigma)) set.seed(4750); Z <- matrix(rnorm(2 * 2000), nrow = 2) X <- t(c(1, 2) + C %*% Z) round(cov(X), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [1,] 0.97 0.74 [2,] 0.74 0.92 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot(X, pch = 20, col = adjustcolor("#003366", .4), asp = 1, xlab = "x1", ylab = "x2") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Limit Theorems (Rizzo 2.5) - **WLLN:** $\bar X_n \xrightarrow{P}\mu$; **SLLN:** $\bar X_n \xrightarrow{a.s.}\mu$ - **CLT:** $\dfrac{\bar X_n-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt n}\xrightarrow{D} N(0,1)$ when $\sigma^2<\infty$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750) par(mfrow = c(1, 4)) for (n in c(1, 5, 30, 100)) { xbar <- colMeans(matrix(rexp(n * 5000), nrow = n)) hist((xbar - 1) / (1 / sqrt(n)), prob = TRUE, breaks = 40, main = paste("n =", n), xlab = "", col = "#FFCC00", xlim = c(-4, 4)) curve(dnorm(x), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "#003366") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: question Repeat with Cauchy data. What breaks, and why? ::: ## Statistics (Rizzo 2.6): ecdf and Quantiles - **ecdf** $F_n(x) = \frac1n\#\{i: x_i\le x\}$ - $q$-quantile: $X_q = \inf\{x: F(x)\ge q\}$; R's default `quantile(type = 7)` assigns $(k-1)/(n-1)$ to $x_{(k)}$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); x <- rnorm(25) plot(ecdf(x), main = "ecdf of 25 N(0,1) draws vs true cdf", col = "#003366", lwd = 2) curve(pnorm(x), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} quantile(x, c(.25, .5, .75)); quantile(x, .5, type = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 25% 50% 75% -0.8428 -0.3289 0.4457 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 50% -0.3289 ``` ::: ::: ## Bias, Standard Error, and MSE - $\bias(\hat\theta) = \E[\hat\theta] - \theta$; unbiased if bias $=0$ - $\se(\hat\theta) = \sqrt{\var(\hat\theta)}$ - $\mse(\hat\theta) = \E[(\hat\theta-\theta)^2] = \var(\hat\theta) + \bias^2(\hat\theta)$ **Example.** For $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, compare $S^2$ (divisor $n-1$) with $\hat\sigma^2$ (divisor $n$): ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); n <- 10; sigma2 <- 4 sims <- replicate(1e5, { x <- rnorm(n, sd = 2); c(S2 = var(x), mle = var(x) * (n - 1) / n) }) rbind(bias = rowMeans(sims) - sigma2, MSE = rowMeans((sims - sigma2)^2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` S2 mle bias -0.006832 -0.4061 MSE 3.547734 3.0386 ``` ::: ::: ::: tip The biased estimator has the **smaller MSE**: the bias-variance trade-off we will see again in ridge regression and Bayes estimators. ::: ## Maximum Likelihood (Examples 2.5 - 2.6) - $L(\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^n f(x_i\mid\theta)$, $\hat\theta = \argmax_\theta \log L(\theta)$ - **Example 2.5:** for $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, $\hat\mu = \bar x$, $\hat\sigma^2 = \frac1n\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2$ - **Invariance (Example 2.6):** if $\hat\theta$ is the MLE of $\theta$, then $g(\hat\theta)$ is the MLE of $g(\theta)$ (e.g. $\hat\sigma = \sqrt{\hat\sigma^2}$) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); x <- rnorm(50, mean = 5, sd = 2) negll <- function(par) -sum(dnorm(x, par[1], exp(par[2]), log = TRUE)) fit <- optim(c(0, 0), negll) c(mu_hat = fit$par[1], sigma_hat = exp(fit$par[2]), closed_form_mu = mean(x), closed_form_sigma = sqrt(mean((x - mean(x))^2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mu_hat sigma_hat closed_form_mu closed_form_sigma 5.224 2.153 5.224 2.154 ``` ::: ::: ::: notes - We parametrize log(sigma) so the optimizer is unconstrained. More on optim in Chapter 14, and on MOM/MLE/Bayes in deck 05. ::: ## Bayes' Theorem and Bayesian Statistics (Rizzo 2.7) $$ \pi(\theta\mid x) = \frac{f(x\mid\theta)\pi(\theta)}{\int f(x\mid\theta)\pi(\theta)\,d\theta} \;\propto\; \text{likelihood}\times\text{prior} $$ **Beta-Binomial:** $X\mid p\sim\text{Bin}(n,p)$, $p\sim\text{Beta}(a,b)$ $\Rightarrow$ $p\mid x\sim\text{Beta}(a+x,\, b+n-x)$. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- 2; b <- 2; n <- 20; xobs <- 14 curve(dbeta(x, a, b), 0, 1, lwd = 3, lty = 2, ylim = c(0, 4.5), ylab = "density", xlab = "p") curve(dbeta(x, a + xobs, b + n - xobs), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "#003366") abline(v = xobs / n, col = "red", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("prior Beta(2,2)", "posterior Beta(16,8)", "MLE 14/20"), lty = c(2, 1, 1), col = c(1, "#003366", "red"), lwd = 3, bty = "n") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Markov Chains (Rizzo 2.8) - $\{X_t\}$ with $P(X_{t+1}=j\mid X_t = i, X_{t-1},\dots) = p_{ij}$; transition matrix $\mathbf P = (p_{ij})$, rows sum to 1 - $n$-step transitions: $\mathbf P^n$; stationary distribution $\boldsymbol\pi^\T = \boldsymbol\pi^\T\mathbf P$ **Example 2.7 (DNA mutation).** $p_{ii} = 1-3\alpha$, $p_{ij} = \alpha$, $\alpha = 0.1$. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} alpha <- 0.1 P <- matrix(alpha, 4, 4); diag(P) <- 1 - 3 * alpha matpow <- function(M, k) Reduce(`%*%`, replicate(k, M, simplify = FALSE)) round(matpow(P, 2), 4); round(matpow(P, 16), 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [1,] 0.52 0.16 0.16 0.16 [2,] 0.16 0.52 0.16 0.16 [3,] 0.16 0.16 0.52 0.16 [4,] 0.16 0.16 0.16 0.52 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [1,] 0.2502 0.2499 0.2499 0.2499 [2,] 0.2499 0.2502 0.2499 0.2499 [3,] 0.2499 0.2499 0.2502 0.2499 [4,] 0.2499 0.2499 0.2499 0.2502 ``` ::: ::: ## Example 2.8: Random Walk $X_{t+1} = X_t + \epsilon_t$, $\epsilon_t = \pm 1$ with probability $1/2$ each. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750) walks <- replicate(5, cumsum(sample(c(-1, 1), 1000, replace = TRUE))) matplot(walks, type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, xlab = "t", ylab = expression(X[t]), main = "Five symmetric random walks") abline(h = 0, lty = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/02-prob-stat/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: notes - Markov chains return in MCMC. Random walks return in Chapter 4 (random processes, Brownian motion). ::: ## Summary ::: instructions - Conditional expectation / variance formulas: verify hierarchical models by simulation. - The `d/p/q/r` functions and the relationships between families. - MVN via Cholesky: our first *generator* recipe (Ch 3). - LLN and CLT explain why Monte Carlo works (Ch 6-7). - Bias / SE / MSE are the yardsticks for every estimator this semester. ::: ::: your-turn **HW 1, Extra Question:** For $X\sim\chi^2(\nu = N+1)$ with $N\sim\text{Poisson}(\lambda)$, find $\E[X]$ and $\var(X)$ using (2.1)-(2.2) *and* by simulation. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
